name: Pink Squirrel
description: Crème de noyaux, crème de cacao, and cream—the Milwaukee dessert classic, built with Baileys tonight.
history: Credited to Bryant’s Cocktail Lounge in Milwaukee in the 1940s. The original is equal parts crème de noyaux, white crème de cacao, and cream. Noyaux is almond-and-stone-fruit, not cherry syrup.
whyItWorks: Noyaux’s almond-cherry-pit note is the pink half; cacao is the chocolate half; cream (or Baileys) binds them into a grasshopper cousin.
steps: Shake crème de noyaux, crème de cacao, and Baileys hard with ice.
techniqueNotes: If you later stock heavy cream, use 1 oz cream instead of Baileys for the original.

recommendedBottles.rationale: The almond-pink bottle the drink is named around.
Cream stand-in from the current bar.

substitutions.notes: Fresh cream is traditional and a little less sweet.
